4521.summary: On macOS and Windows, a community renamed only by case keeps its wiki page, and the index link still works.
4521.why: On macOS and Windows, groups.md and Groups.md are the same file. When a community's label changed from groups to Groups, graphify wrote the page, then the end-of-run cleanup deleted it, because it compared file names with case. index.md kept linking to the deleted page.
4521.what: The cleanup now compares files by identity (device and inode), not by name. A page written in this run is kept and renamed to the new case. A stale page that is a separate file is still removed.
4521.helps: Anyone on macOS or Windows who re-exports a wiki after a community label changes only in case.

4326.summary: Graphify now gives a node and its edges the same key when it runs from a subfolder, so edges stop landing on the wrong node.
4326.why: Run from a subfolder like root/firmware, the renamed x.html node got a new id but its edges did not. By dedup time source_file is already relative to the root, yet _rank_path still called .resolve(), which adds the current folder in front.
4326.what: _rank_path now resolves only absolute paths. The node key and the edge key are both firmware/lib/portal.html, so the edge lands on firmware_lib_portal_html.
4326.helps: Anyone who runs graphify from a subfolder. Their edges stay on the renamed node, and which node wins a collision no longer depends on where graphify started.

  B --> BE["edge lands on firmware_lib_portal"]:::bad
  P -- "now: kept as is" --> G["node key firmware/lib/portal.html"]:::good

4371.summary: The id-collision warning now says what the merge did, instead of claiming a document was lost.
4371.why: The warning told every user that "the dropped node is lost" and that the id "does not identify a single entity". On the reporter's corpus that was wrong. None of their 16 remaining warnings was a lost document. Each was one entity described in two files, or a reference to another file, and merging was correct.
4371.what: The warning now names the node it kept and the node it merged into it. The next sentence depends on where the id came from: a file path (a reference to the kept file, or a separate document) or neither (probably one entity described in both files). Which node survives does not change. The tests are written so this PR and #4410 pass in either merge order (141 passed in tests/test_dedup.py with both applied).
4371.helps: Anyone reading the collision warning gets text that matches what the merge did. The severity stays WARNING.
4371.before: [graphify] WARNING: node 'sender' is minted by two different files — keeping 'Sender' from 'docs/a.md', dropping 'sender service' from 'docs/b.md'. An ID is derived from the source path plus the entity name, so this one does not identify a single entity and the dropped node is lost.
4371.after: [graphify] WARNING: node 'sender' is minted by two different files: kept 'Sender' from 'docs/a.md', merged 'sender service' from 'docs/b.md' into it. The id comes from neither path, so this is probably one entity described in both files. The merged node's own label and attributes are not kept; its edges stay on the kept node.
limits: The text cannot tell a reference from a second document when the id comes from a path. It says both are possible. Telling them apart needs edge evidence and is out of scope here: #4362 (v0.9.88) and #4410 resolve the cases they can, and this warning covers the collisions they leave, such as docs/protocol.md with its own page that also mints the bare id of a top-level protocol.md.
"Probably one entity" for an id that comes from neither path is an inference, not a fact. Two real documents can also share such an id; the merged node's label and attributes are then lost.
Severity stays WARNING. The reporter asked for something milder, but test_issue_3472 asserts WARNING for a non-path id, so lowering it would change an existing test.
4371.diagram:
flowchart LR
  C["two files mint the same id"] --> Q("where does the id come from?")
  Q -- "a file path" --> Y["warning: a reference to the kept file, or a separate document"]
  Q -- "neither path" --> N["warning: probably one entity described in both files"]
  Y --> S["same node survives as before"]:::same
  N --> S

4362.summary: When a dropped folder makes two real documents share one bare id, each gets its own path-qualified id. A mere reference to another document stays one node.
4362.why: Semantic extraction sometimes drops the folder from an id, so a/x.md and b/x.md both emit x. Dedup merged them and one real document was lost.
4362.what: When files with different paths share a bare id, each file's node is renamed to its path-qualified id (a_x, b_x). The exception is a bare id that only mentions another document: a node that another node of its own file points to with a references edge, and whose id is a shorter slice of its file path. Mentions also lose ties in the collision ranking, so a real document beats them.
4362.helps: Two real documents with the same bare id stay two nodes instead of one being dropped. A reference to another document no longer becomes a second document or a self-link.
4362.before: a/x.md emits x and b/x.md emits x: dedup keeps one node and b/x.md is dropped (one real document lost).
4362.after: a/x.md emits x and b/x.md emits x: two nodes, a_x and b_x, with edges following their own file.
limits: The mention evidence is inferred from the edges an LLM chose to emit. A missing or reversed references edge gives no evidence, so both files are renamed (R_noedge). With a reversed edge, the reference can still end up as a self-link.
A real document whose own node is linked to its file-level id the same way (an entity named like its file) reads as a mention, and that collision collapses as on v8.
R_toplevel stays wrong: with a top-level protocol.md that also mints protocol, one real document is still dropped by the label tiebreak. It is a separate collision, and a test pins today's result.

If two or more other files also mint the mention's id, the mention stays on the bare id and build_from_json folds it into its own file's page, which gives a self-link and no warning. This is the same outcome as the first version of this PR.
A reference to the bare id from a third file (c.md -> x) cannot be attributed to one file. The edge is left on x, one warning is printed per id, and build() then drops it because no node x exists.

For imports, imports_from and re_exports edges, build_from_json mints an external stub node for the missing target. An import-family edge to a renamed bare id leaves a phantom external node x. Checked by hand; there is no test.

Absolute source_file values (no root, outside the root, or a Windows path on POSIX) are never qualified, so checkout paths cannot leak into ids (#502, #2197, #2618). Those collisions stay on collapse-and-warn.
AST-tier nodes are not touched. Hyperedge members given as dicts are not rewritten, as in the #4282 pass.

cases.correct: 2 nodes; the firmware doc references docs/protocol.md
cases.before: ok, because the mention's label is shorter

cases.correct: no x; c.md's edge not pinned on one file
cases.before: c_note pinned on a_x as EXTRACTED, b/x.md dropped

flowchart LR
  A["a/x.md emits id x"] --> Q("both use the bare id x")
  B["b/x.md emits id x"] --> Q
  Q -- "v8" --> V["one node x, b/x.md is lost"]:::bad

4353.summary: Step 1 of /graphify now fails loudly when it cannot save its files, and every reader keeps the saved folder name exactly. Stacked on #4344: review that first, the last 4 commits here are this PR's own.
4353.why: On a full disk, Step 1 left .graphify_python and .graphify_root empty and still exited 0. The next step then failed with "bash: : command not found", and graphify update rebuilt the current folder instead of the project. Six readers also trimmed spaces from the saved folder, so "proj " came back as "proj".
4353.what: Step 1 writes each file to a temp file and renames it into place. If anything fails, it cleans up, names the file and exits 1. A new read_root_marker() strips only a byte-order mark and one final newline. graphify update, build.py, watch.py, reflect.py and the git hooks all use it, and so does read_scan_root() from #4344, so there is one rule for reading the marker.
4353.helps: Anyone whose disk fills up during Step 1 gets a clear error at that step, not a confusing failure one step later. Anyone with a trailing space in a folder name gets that folder from graphify update.

  participant D as graphify-out
  participant N as Next step

  D-->>S: write fails, file left empty

4353.after: Step 1 with a full disk: "could not write graphify-out/.graphify_python (File too large; is the disk full?)", exit code 1, no files left behind.

4344.summary: Skill scripts read the scan folder, community names and spec path from files the agent writes, instead of pasting them into code.
4344.why: The skill told the agent to paste the scan folder, the community names and the spec path into python -c scripts, so a value could become code. A folder named proj$(touch PWNED) ran touch PWNED before Python started. A label with a quote could end the Python string early. A scan path with a line break could end the heredoc early, and the rest of the path would run as shell. This was reported in a comment on #4309.
4344.what: The agent now writes each value to a file in graphify-out/ through a quoted heredoc, and the script reads that file. A new read_scan_root() reads the saved folder. The interpreter path is quoted in every skill script. Step 1 tells the agent to refuse a scan path with a line break and ask for another, and the Python side rejects multi-line input.
4344.helps: Anyone who runs /graphify on a folder whose name contains shell syntax, or on a path with spaces, no longer runs that name as a command. The scan also stops picking the wrong folder.
4344.diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant A as Agent
  participant Sh as Shell
  participant P as Python script
  participant F as graphify-out file
  rect rgba(212, 76, 71, 0.10)
  Note over A,F: Before
  A->>Sh: python -c with the folder name pasted in
  Sh->>Sh: expands proj$(touch PWNED) and runs touch
  Sh->>P: start with the wrong folder
  end
  rect rgba(68, 131, 97, 0.10)
  Note over A,F: After
  A->>F: write the folder name with a quoted heredoc
  A->>Sh: run the script, nothing pasted
  Sh->>P: start
  P->>F: read the folder name as data
  end

4344.after: This branch, same folder: nothing is created, Detected 1 files.

4410.summary: docs/protocol.md keeps its own node when a top-level protocol.md mints the same bare id, and the real top-level file wins the collapse whatever the labels are.
4410.why: When the model drops the folder, protocol.md, docs/protocol.md and docs/firmware/protocol.md all mint protocol. #4362 skips any group whose bare id names an input file, because the id may be a reference to it. The collapse then ran and one real document was dropped. The maintainer named this gap when reviewing #4371.
4410.what: The file whose full stem is the id (protocol.md) keeps it. Each other file with that bare id is decided on its own. With no node spelled like its own full stem, the bare id is its page and is renamed (docs_protocol). With one, the bare id may be a reference and collapses as before. A bare path slice from a file with its own page also ranks as a reference, so protocol.md's node survives whatever the label lengths are.
4410.helps: Anyone with a top-level README or protocol.md next to a docs/ copy of the same name. No document is silently dropped, and a reference to the top-level file lands on it.
4410.before: protocol.md + docs/protocol.md + docs/firmware/protocol.md: nodes docs_protocol, docs_firmware_protocol. protocol.md has no node; the firmware reference ends on docs_protocol.
4410.after: Same input: nodes protocol (protocol.md), docs_protocol, docs_firmware_protocol. The firmware reference ends on protocol.

  Q -- "yes: may be a reference" --> C["collapses onto protocol.md"]:::same
  T["protocol.md mints protocol"] --> K["keeps protocol"]:::good

4434.summary: Tell the model the real node-id rule and hand it each file's stem, so a non-ASCII path gets one stable id prefix.
4434.why: The extraction prompts said ids use only [a-z0-9_], but ids.py keeps Unicode letters (docs/tz/ЛЗ4.md becomes docs_tz_лз4). The model could not follow both, so it invented a different stem per chunk and per run, and _semantic_id_remap reconciled none of them.
4434.what: The rule in llm.py and both extraction-spec fragments now says what ids.py does: letters and digits of any script are kept, every other run of characters becomes one _. A new helper, file_id_stem, computes each file's stem in code. graphify extract adds it to the prompt as stem="...", and the skill writes a path<TAB>stem file that the agent copies into each subagent's file list.
4434.helps: Anyone whose docs have Cyrillic, CJK or accented file names. Every node from such a file is told the same prefix that the document pass already uses for the file's own node.

  S --> B["skill: path TAB stem file list"]:::good
  A --> N["model copies the stem as id prefix"]
  B --> N

4452.summary: A symbol that spells a sibling file's old id (const sql in x.mjs next to x.sql) keeps its own node, so the file node is no longer relabelled.
4452.why: extract() renames each file's old id, which is its path with the extension (esquema_x_sql for x.sql), to the final id. It does this on every node, edge end and raw call that spells it. The JS variable sql in x.mjs is minted with the same string, so it took the file node's id and dedup dropped one of the two. The x.mjs file node ended up labelled sql, and graphify explain "x.mjs" found nothing.
4452.what: A key is renamed only for the file that minted it, and only when another file's own symbol carries the same id. Nodes, edge ends and raw calls each follow the file they belong to. Every other key renames as before. Swift extension ids and Objective-C field tables follow the same rule.
4452.helps: Anyone with a script next to a same-stem file, such as a migration runner foo.mjs beside foo.sql that uses a client named sql. The file node keeps its filename and the variable gets its own id.
4452.diagram:
flowchart LR

  Q -- "x.sql, its own file" --> R["renamed to esquema_x"]:::good
  Q -- "sql variable in x.mjs" --> S["kept as esquema_x_sql"]:::good
  Q -- "file that only refers to x.sql" --> R

5 nodes, 4 edges

esquema_x_mjs_esquema_x | sql   <- should be the file node x.mjs
4452.after:
6 nodes, 5 edges, no note

esquema_x_sql           | sql

4462.summary: Dropping the backticks stops bash from running commands inside the merge, so Part C and the update merge hand Python exactly the code shown.
4462.why: With graphify installed, Part C ran a full graphify update in the middle of the merge and rewrote graph.json. The update output landed in the Python source, so Part C failed with SyntaxError and .graphify_extract.json was never written. Without graphify on PATH, bash only printed command not found, so nobody noticed.
4462.what: Four comment lines lose their backticks and keep their words: three Part C lines and one update merge line. The skills are regenerated from the fixed fragments, with one gen.py audit line updated to match. A new test scans every generated skill two ways: a static check for backticks inside double-quoted -c blocks, and a runtime check that runs each Part C and merge statement under bash with a fake graphify and a fake changed first on PATH.
4462.helps: Anyone who runs Part C or the update merge with graphify installed. No stray update rewrites their graph.json, and the merge runs to the end.
4462.diagram:
flowchart LR
  C["comment with backticks in a -c block"] --> B["bash expands it before Python starts"]:::bad
  B --> R["graphify update runs, its output lands in the code"]:::bad
  R --> E["SyntaxError, no .graphify_extract.json"]:::bad
  C --> G["backticks dropped, the comment passes through"]:::good
  G --> M["the merge runs"]:::good
4462.before: Part C on v8 with graphify on PATH: exit 1, SyntaxError, graph.json rewritten by the unrequested update, .graphify_extract.json not written.
4462.after: Same run on this branch: exit 0, Merged: 1 nodes, 0 edges, graph.json unchanged, .graphify_extract.json written (237 bytes).
limits: The runtime check runs only $(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python) -c "..." statements in fenced bash blocks. Other shapes such as "$PYTHON" -c "..." are not run, though the static check still scans them.
$VAR expansion inside the quotes is not a command, so neither check looks at it.

The windows monolith Part C sits in a PowerShell here-string, so the runtime check skips it on purpose and the runtime test skips on win32.

4476.summary: Removing one MERGE_HEAD check lets the post-merge hook rebuild the graph after every real merge, not only fast-forwards.
4476.why: After git merge --no-ff, a merge of diverged branches, or git pull, the hook printed nothing and graph.json kept the old code. The hook exits if .git/MERGE_HEAD exists, and git 2.54 still has that file on disk while post-merge runs. It deletes it only after the hook returns.
4476.what: The MERGE_HEAD check is gone from the post-merge script only, and the comment that said MERGE_HEAD was already gone is corrected. The same check stays in post-commit and post-checkout, where it keeps those hooks quiet during a conflicted merge.
4476.helps: Anyone with graphify hooks installed who merges or pulls. The background rebuild now runs after the merge, so the #2418 cleanup of symbols brought back by the union merge driver also runs.
4476.diagram:
flowchart LR
  M["git merge --no-ff / git pull"] --> H["post-merge runs, MERGE_HEAD still on disk"]
  H --> X["v8: MERGE_HEAD check exits"]:::bad
  X --> S["graph.json stays stale"]:::bad
  H --> F["this PR: no MERGE_HEAD check"]:::good
  F --> R["background rebuild launches"]:::good
limits: Hooks already installed keep the old check until the user re-runs graphify hook install.
If an older git deletes MERGE_HEAD before running post-merge, the new test passes there even without the fix. Which git versions do that is not checked.
The full test suite was not run, only tests/test_hooks.py (147 passed).

4491.summary: The hooks now rebuild the graph once after a clean cherry-pick, a rebase, a pull --rebase, or a range pick or revert, instead of never.
4491.why: After a clean git cherry-pick, git rebase or git pull --rebase, no rebuild ran and graph.json kept the old code. post-commit exited on CHERRY_PICK_HEAD, which git leaves on disk while the hook runs. During a rebase every hook skips while rebase-merge/ exists, and graphify installed no post-rewrite hook to rebuild at the end.
4491.what: post-commit no longer checks CHERRY_PICK_HEAD. During a range pick or revert it skips every step but the last, then rebuilds once from sequencer/head so every picked commit is covered. A stale sequencer/ left by git reset --hard is ignored. A new post-rewrite hook rebuilds after a rebase and ignores amend.
4491.helps: Anyone with graphify hooks who cherry-picks, rebases or pulls with --rebase. The graph matches the code after the operation, and a tracked graph.json is never rewritten between picks, so git never refuses the next pick.
4491.diagram:
flowchart LR
  P["cherry-pick / rebase finishes"] --> V["v8: CHERRY_PICK_HEAD or rebase-merge/ still on disk"]:::bad
  V --> S["every hook exits, graph stale"]:::bad
  P --> F["post-commit: last sequencer step / post-rewrite: rebase"]:::good
  F --> R["one rebuild covering the whole operation"]:::good
4491.before:
git cherry-pick side   -> 0 rebuilds
git rebase main        -> 0 rebuilds
git commit (control)   -> 1 rebuild
4491.after:
git cherry-pick side   -> 1 rebuild
git rebase main        -> 1 rebuild
git commit (control)   -> 1 rebuild
limits: --skip on the last pick and --quit still leave the graph stale, as on v8: git runs no hook when a sequence ends that way.
Editing the commit message while resolving a pick, or reverting a Revert "..." commit, makes that step rebuild mid-sequence. Inferred from the logic, not tested.
Hooks already installed keep the old behaviour until graphify hook install is run again.
Windows and a clean range racing the rebuild were not tested.

4520.summary: explain and path now name the repo of each candidate when two merged files share a basename, instead of calling both one file.
4520.why: In a merged graph, web/dup.py and ml/dup.py are both stored as dup.py. The same-file check compared that bare name, so both nodes looked like one file. explain and path then said "matches 2 nodes in dup.py", listed two bare L1 lines, and gave a hint that could not tell them apart.
4520.what: A file is now its repo plus its source_file. When candidates span more than one repo, the refusal shows web/dup.py and ml/dup.py. When the same path exists in two repos, the hint says so and asks for the full node id.
4520.helps: Anyone who merges repos that share file names such as dup.py, __init__.py or index.ts. The refusal now shows which repo each candidate came from, and the node-id retry is clear.

  subgraph Before
    A1["web/dup.py"] --> K1["key: dup.py"]
    A2["ml/dup.py"] --> K1
    K1 --> M1["one file: 'matches 2 nodes in dup.py'"]:::bad
  end

    B1["web/dup.py"] --> K2["key: web + dup.py"]
    B2["ml/dup.py"] --> K3["key: ml + dup.py"]

proposals.title: Let code make node ids, not the LLM
proposals.problem: graphify can drop a real file from the graph without an error. When two nodes get the same id, dedup keeps one. For docs the LLM types the id, gets it wrong in repeatable ways, and nothing checks it.
proposals.evidence: On 0.9.89, a/x.md and a/x.html with the same id x lose a/x.html. In #4432 the model invents a different stem in each chunk for Cyrillic paths. The same cause is behind #4281, #3947, #3407 and #1829. Numbers from a real repo are coming in stage 0.

parts.label: 1. A file disappears
parts.md:
Put two files in one folder, `a/x.md` and `a/x.html`. The LLM gives a node from each the id `x`. On 0.9.89 the graph keeps `a/x.md` and drops `a/x.html`:

```text
input:   a/x.md   -> id x
         a/x.html -> id x
output:  a_x  (a/x.md)
         a/x.html is gone, one warning on stderr
```

An agent reading the graph has no way to know `a/x.html` existed. It answers without it.

parts.label: 2. Why: dedup trusts the id
parts.md:
Dedup (`deduplicate_entities`, `dedup.py:885`) has one rule: two nodes with the same id are the same thing, so it keeps one and drops the other.

That rule is only safe if the id is right every time. Two different things must never get the same id, and the same thing must get the same id on every run. When an id is wrong, dedup can't tell, and a real node is dropped.

parts.label: 3. Where the id comes from
parts.md:
For code, `make_id()` in `ids.py` builds the id from the file path and the symbol name. It is deterministic, but it throws away the file extension and the difference between `/` and `_`, so `x.py` and `x.html` both start from `x`.

For docs and concepts, the LLM types the id. The prompt (`llm.py:520`) tells it to write `{path}_{name}` using only `[a-z0-9_]`. So the model has to slug a path exactly like `ids.py` does, repeat it the same way in every chunk and every run, and invent ids for nodes in files it can't see. It gets this wrong in a few repeatable ways:
parts.diagram:
flowchart TD P["prompt: write the id as path_name"] --> L{"LLM"} L -->|right| OK["docs_firmware_protocol"]:::good L -->|drops the folder| A["protocol
#4281"]:::bad L -->|path is Cyrillic, rule says a-z| B["invents a stem per chunk
#4432"]:::bad L -->|points at another file| C["guesses that file's id
#3947"]:::bad OK --> D["dedup trusts every one of these"] A --> D B --> D C --> D
parts.caption: The same prompt rule produces right and wrong ids, and dedup can't tell them apart

parts.label: 4. Why fixing each case doesn't end it
parts.md:
So far each fix has repaired one shape after the fact, inside dedup: one pass for an extension clash, one for a dropped folder (#4362), one for a top-level file (#4410). Each pass assumes the other problem isn't there, so a file with both problems falls through both. That is the `a/x.md` + `a/x.html` case above. A test that generates random file trees found it on its first run.

Repairing ids before dedup doesn't work either. I tried rebuilding every id from its `source_file`. It passed 3 of 7 cases, because the model sometimes puts the wrong `source_file` on a node that only mentions another file.

The same cause shows up in many open issues: #4281, #4432, #3947, #3407, #1829, #3726, #3568, #3257 and more. Roughly 30 issues and PRs come back to it.
parts.diagram:
flowchart LR
  IN["ids, some wrong"]:::bad --> P1["fix extension clash"]
  P1 --> P2["fix dropped folder"]
  P2 --> P3["fix top-level file"]
  P3 --> P4["next shape"]:::bad
  P4 --> DROP["drop on same id"]
parts.caption: Each repair handles one shape. New shapes keep getting through

parts.label: 5. The fix: code makes the id, the model only names
parts.md:
Three rules, each borrowed from a system that already solved this:

1. **Code makes every id.** The model returns a short name and picks its file from a list (`f1`, `f2`). Code builds the id from the file and the name. My code index, symbolgraph, works this way: the id is made in code, and identity is a key of full path, kind and name that keeps the extension.
2. **A mention of another file is a reference, not a node.** The model writes the name it is pointing at. A resolver links it once all files are extracted. Compilers and code indexers (LSP, SCIP) work this way: using a name never creates a symbol.
3. **Dedup merges on that full key and reports conflicts.** Databases do this: a unique key that clashes is an error, not a silent overwrite.

What the model would return:

```json
// today: the model types global ids
{"nodes":[{"id":"docs_firmware_protocol_handshake","source_file":"docs/firmware/protocol.md"}],
 "edges":[{"source":"docs_firmware_protocol_handshake","target":"protocol"}]}

// proposed: names, a file picked from a list, and an explicit reference
{"nodes":[{"name":"handshake","file":"f1","kind":"concept"}],
 "edges":[{"source":"handshake","target_ref":{"name":"protocol","file_hint":"docs/protocol.md"}}]}
```

The model can still pick the wrong file or name. The difference is that the mistake shows up as an unresolved or ambiguous reference instead of a node that quietly disappears.
parts.diagram:
flowchart TD LLM["LLM returns names,
a file from the list,
and references"] --> MINT["code builds id and key"]:::good AST["AST extractors"] --> TABLE["table of every node, by key"] MINT --> TABLE LLM --> REFS["references"] TABLE --> RES["resolver"]:::good REFS --> RES RES -->|one match| E["edge"] RES -->|several| AMB["AMBIGUOUS edge"] RES -->|none| UN["unresolved, reported"] TABLE --> DD["dedup on key,
conflict reported"]:::good
parts.caption: Proposed: the model names things, code builds ids, references are resolved at the end

parts.label: 6. What it costs
parts.md:
- Any prompt change re-runs semantic extraction once for every user, because the cache key includes a prompt fingerprint (`cache.py:162`). Grouping the prompt changes pays this once.
- The id rule is written in `llm.py` and in the skillgen fragments, so each step touches both.
- Stage 4 changes ids in saved graphs. It needs a graph format version and a remap, like `_semantic_id_remap` already does for old ids.

parts.label: 7. Questions for you
parts.md:
1. Do you agree with the direction: code makes ids, the model names and picks, mentions are references?
2. Would you review stages 0 to 3 as separate small PRs?
3. For stage 4, is a graph format version fine, or do old ids have to keep working?
4. Is a property test of about 4 seconds fine in CI, or should it run nightly?

plan: Stage 0: a test that generates random file trees and checks that every file keeps a node, plus a count of how many LLM ids miss their file's path on a real repo. Easy to undo.
Stage 1: code computes each file's path stem and puts it in the prompt, and the prompt rule matches ids.py (my #4432 PR). Easy to undo.
Stage 2: the model picks its file from a list and returns a short name. Code builds the id. The old output format is still accepted. Easy to undo.
Stage 3: a mention of another file becomes a reference, linked after extraction, behind a flag. Easy to undo.
Stage 4: dedup merges on a full key (path with extension, kind, name) and reports conflicts. Changes saved ids, so I'd only start after you agree.
Stage 5: keep ids the same across --update by matching old and new keys.

proposals.title: Make indexing cheaper, faster and safer without a rewrite
proposals.problem: On big repos with many users, graphify pays the LLM again on every machine for the same doc, re-bills a whole big doc for a one-line edit, runs most steps after parsing on one core, and can drop a node or an edge without an error.
proposals.evidence: From the code on 0.9.92 (86c57be8): the semantic cache sits in each checkout (cache.py:1015); its key is the whole file's hash even for sliced docs (cache.py:511); the model is not in the key; --update copies edges of unchanged files without re-resolving them (watch.py:1981); same-id nodes overwrite each other with nothing counted (build.py:9-16); graph.json writes schema_version but nothing reads it (export.py:476). No cost or time numbers yet: stage 0 measures them.

parts.label: 1. What goes wrong
parts.md:
Three things get worse as a repo and its team grow.

- **LLM cost.** Every laptop and every CI runner pays for the same unchanged doc, because the semantic cache lives inside each checkout.
- **Time.** Parsing runs on all cores, but the steps after it (resolving calls, dedup, clustering, writing files) run on one core.
- **Wrong graphs with no error.** When two different things get the same id, one is dropped and nothing counts it. After a commit, an unchanged file that calls a newly added function may get no edge to it (suspected, test pending).

I have no numbers yet for any of these. Stage 0 below measures them before anything changes.
parts.diagram:
flowchart LR DOC["docs/guide.md
unchanged"] --> A["laptop A
cache miss, LLM call"]:::bad DOC --> B["laptop B
cache miss, LLM call"]:::bad DOC --> C["CI runner
cache miss, LLM call"]:::bad A --> CA["graphify-out/cache on A"] B --> CB["graphify-out/cache on B"] C --> CC["graphify-out/cache on CI"] classDef bad fill:#fde2e1,stroke:#c0392b,color:#111
parts.caption: Today: three machines pay the LLM for the same unchanged doc

parts.label: 2. Why it happens
parts.md:
Each problem has one cause in the code (references are to 0.9.92, `86c57be8`):

| Problem | Cause | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Same doc billed on every machine | the semantic cache folder sits under `graphify-out/` in each checkout | `cache_dir`, `cache.py:1015` |
| A typo re-bills a whole big doc | big docs are split into slices, but the cache key is the hash of the whole file | `file_hash`, `cache.py:511`; `file_slice.py` |
| Switching models replays old output | the model is not part of the cache key and not stored with the entry | `cache.py` |
| Missing call edge after a commit | `--update` re-reads changed files only; edges of unchanged files are copied, never re-resolved. #2406 fixed the other direction | `watch.py:1981` |
| Silent drop on the same id | the last node with an id overwrites the first, by design, with nothing counted | `build.py:9-16`, `dedupe_nodes` `build.py:886` |
| Slow on big repos | only parsing is parallel | `_extract_parallel`, `extract.py:8949` |
| No safe way to change ids | `graph.json` stores `schema_version`, but no reader checks it | `export.py:176`, `export.py:476` |

parts.label: 3. How a commit can miss an edge
parts.md:
This is the correctness gap I suspect, not one I've proven. A test that compares `--update` with a full rebuild will settle it.

Renames are fine: if you rename `foo` and fix its callers in the same commit, both files are re-read. The gap is a name that **appears** or **moves** while its caller stays untouched.
parts.diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant Dev as Developer
  participant Hook as post-commit hook
  participant Ex as extract
  participant Old as saved graph.json
  Dev->>Hook: commit adds def foo in b.py
  Hook->>Ex: re-extract b.py only
  Ex-->>Hook: new node foo
  Hook->>Old: copy edges of unchanged a.py
  Note over Old: a.py already called foo, but its call was unresolved last time
  Hook-->>Dev: graph has foo, no edge from a.py to foo
  Note over Dev,Old: a full rebuild would have the edge
parts.caption: The caller in a.py is never re-read, so its call to the new foo stays unresolved

parts.label: 4. How this affects the project
parts.md:
- Teams pay per person, not per repo. Ten people on one docs-heavy repo pay about ten times.
- An agent answers from the graph with confidence. A dropped node or a missing edge turns into a wrong answer, not an error.
- Id bugs get fixed one shape at a time (#4449, #4432, #4362, #4410), because no check shows how many collisions there are.
- Any change to the prompt or to ids resets every user's cache, so the fixes that matter most are also the most expensive to ship.

parts.label: 5. The fix, part 1: share the cache and cache by slice
parts.md:
Two ideas from build tools (Bazel, sccache, restic):

1. **A shared, content-addressed cache.** A setting points graphify at a shared folder. CI writes to it. Laptops only read. The key is the file's content hash, so a changed file can never match a stale entry.
2. **Cache each slice of a big doc by its own hash**, with slices that break at headings. An edit then re-bills only the slice it is in.

Small extra: store the model name with each entry and warn when it differs. The key stays the same, so nobody's cache is lost.
parts.diagram:
sequenceDiagram
  participant CI as CI job on main
  participant S as shared cache folder
  participant Dev as developer laptop
  participant LLM as LLM API
  CI->>LLM: extract docs that miss
  LLM-->>CI: nodes and edges
  CI->>S: write entries, key is content hash
  Dev->>S: read entry for docs/guide.md
  S-->>Dev: hit, no LLM call
  Dev->>LLM: only files the developer changed
  Note over Dev,S: laptops read only, so they cannot poison the shared folder
parts.caption: CI fills the shared folder once; laptops read it and pay only for their own edits

parts.label: 6. Slices today vs proposed
parts.diagram:
flowchart TD F["handbook.md, 300 pages"] --> T{"today: key is hash of whole file"} T -->|typo on page 2| ALL["send every slice again"]:::bad F --> P{"proposed: key is hash of each slice,
slices break at headings"} P -->|typo on page 2| ONE["send slice 1 only,
other slices hit the cache"]:::good classDef bad fill:#fde2e1,stroke:#c0392b,color:#111 classDef good fill:#dff3e4,stroke:#2e7d32,color:#111
parts.caption: Slice-level keys make the cost of an edit follow the edit, not the file

parts.label: 7. The fix, part 2: correctness and speed
parts.md:
- **Count collisions first, change nothing.** Log and report how often two different things share an id. That gives real numbers for the node-identity proposal.
- **Re-resolve only when names change.** Store the set of top-level names each file defines. When a commit adds or moves a name, re-resolve the unchanged files whose unresolved calls use it. Body-only edits do no extra work.
- **Speed up the one-core steps** only where the benchmark points, and only in ways that leave `graph.json` byte-identical. Starting Leiden from the last run's communities changes output, so it goes behind a flag.

parts.label: 8. The order, and why
parts.md:
Changes that keep ids and the prompt as they are ship first, as small PRs that are easy to undo. Changes to ids, the prompt, slice breaks and the `graph.json` layout ship **once**, together, so users pay the cache reset one time.

Before that release, a small PR makes readers check `schema_version`, so older graphify versions refuse a newer graph instead of misreading it. The release then ships a translator from old ids to new ids, like `_semantic_id_remap` (`build.py:963`) did after #1504, so saved graphs and cached LLM output carry over without new LLM calls.
parts.diagram:
flowchart LR M["0. measure
benchmark script"] --> C["1. correctness
no id or prompt change"] C --> K["2. cost and time
no id or prompt change"] K --> V["3. one breaking release
ids, prompt, slices, format
with version and translator"]:::oneway classDef oneway fill:#fff4d6,stroke:#b7791f,color:#111
parts.caption: Two-way doors first, one batched one-way door last

parts.label: 9. What I'm doing now
parts.md:
Nothing is built yet. The first piece is a benchmark script that lives outside graphify, so it needs no PR. It runs the CLI on three repos:

| Repo | Why |
|---|---|
| graphify itself | mid size, easy to check by hand |
| kubernetes | about 15k Go files, no LLM cost, shows where the time goes |
| fastapi `docs/en` | real prose, shows where the LLM cost goes |

It records time per step, tokens split by cache hit and miss, nodes lost in dedup, and `graph.json` size per field. The paid run is capped at $5. I'll post the numbers here before opening any PR.

parts.label: 10. Questions for you
parts.md:
1. Is a shared cache folder that CI writes and laptops read something you'd take, or would you rather keep the cache per checkout?
2. Would you review the report-only collision count and the `schema_version` check as two small PRs?
3. For the breaking release: v1 graphs keep working with a warning for two minor releases. Is that long enough?
4. Is there a repo you'd rather I benchmark than kubernetes and fastapi?

plan: Stage 0: benchmark script outside graphify, CLI only, three repos, LLM spend capped at $5. Numbers posted here first.
Stage 1: count id collisions in the log and the report. Graph output unchanged. Easy to undo.
Stage 1: a test that compares --update with a full rebuild for: a new function an unchanged file calls, a function moved behind a re-export, and a body-only edit.
Stage 1: readers check schema_version and refuse a newer graph with a clear message. Easy to undo.
Stage 2: a shared semantic cache folder, read-only by default, written by CI. Model stored with each entry, with a warning on mismatch. Easy to undo.
Stage 2: if stage 1's test shows the gap, re-resolve unchanged files whose unresolved calls use a name that was added or moved.
Stage 2: speed up the one-core steps the benchmark points at, with a byte-identical graph.json test. Leiden warm start behind a flag.

Stage 3, one release: new ids (see the node-identity proposal), slice-level cache with heading breaks, a smaller graph.json layout, schema_version 2 and an old-to-new id translator. Only after you agree.
